requests.brief: New sim, to be built by sim-builder as our own bundle; no PhET code, art or layout (PhET sims are CC BY-NC 4.0). Concept: phy.rotational-motion.rotational-dynamics.core.rotational-equations. Learning goal: pull a cord wound round a wheel on a fixed frictionless axle and see that the torque FR gives an angular acceleration FR / I, that a ring (I = M R^2) speeds up half as fast as a disc (I = M R^2 / 2) of the same mass and radius, and that the work done by the pull, F times the length of cord unwound, equals the rotational kinetic energy I omega^2 / 2. Model: tau = F R, alpha = tau / I, theta = length / R, omega^2 = 2 alpha theta, K = I omega^2 / 2. Params: mass (kg, 1 to 40, default 20), radius (m, 0.05 to 0.5, default 0.2), pull (N, 1 to 50, default 25), ring (1 for a thin ring, 0 for a uniform disc, default 0). Controls: sliders for mass, radius and pull, a two-way switch for disc or ring, start, pause, reset. Show the cord length unwound, the angular speed, and bars for the work done and the kinetic energy, each with a text label and value (not colour alone). Background art, if any, comes from visual-director, not drawn in the sim. Readouts the card reads: alpha (rad/s^2), omega (rad/s), kinetic_energy (J) after the cord length set in the sim (default 2 m). Card tasks: disc, 20 kg, 0.2 m, 25 N: alpha 12.5 rad/s^2; same after 2 m: kinetic_energy 50 J; ring, same values: alpha 6.25 rad/s^2. Model tests: these values, which are NCERT Example 6.12. Reduced motion: no spinning animation; update the readouts and a still wheel at once.
